dedicated_endpoint_enabled.description: If true, the endpoint will be exposed through a dedicated DNS [Endpoint.dedicated_endpoint_dns]. Your request to the dedicated DNS will be isolated from other users' traffic and will have better performance and reliability. Note: Once you enabled dedicated endpoint, you won't be able to send request to the shared DNS {region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com. The limitation will be removed soon.
dedicated_endpoint_enabled.rationale: Enabling a dedicated endpoint isolates the prediction traffic and DNS from the shared multi-tenant Vertex AI domain. A generic policy can enforce this to reduce the attack surface and prevent noisy-neighbor security risks for sensitive model deployments.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls resource destructibility. Enforcing a 'PREVENT' policy directly improves the availability pillar of security by safeguarding critical ML infrastructure against accidental or malicious deletion.

description.rationale: This is a purely informational text field used for documentation and resource management. It has no effect on the operational security posture, access controls, or network exposure of the endpoint.

display_name.description: Required. The display name of the Endpoint. The name can be up to 128 characters long and can consist of any UTF-8 characters.
display_name.rationale: This argument only controls the human-readable name of the resource for UI and management purposes. It does not configure any access controls, network boundaries, or encryption settings.

labels.description:
The labels with user-defined metadata to organize your Endpoints. Label keys and values can be no longer than 64 characters (Unicode codepoints), can only contain lowercase letters, numeric characters, underscores and dashes. International characters are allowed. See https://goo.gl/xmQnxf for more information and examples of labels.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels provide organizational metadata. While they might be consumed by external IAM conditions, the labels argument itself does not directly enforce security boundaries, network isolation, or encryption on the resource.

location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.description: The resource name of the Endpoint. The name must be numeric with no leading zeros and can be at most 10 digits.
name.rationale: This argument specifies the numeric identifier for the endpoint resource. It is purely an operational naming convention. Enforcing a generic constraint on it does not alter the security posture, data protection, or access boundaries of the deployment.

network.description: The full name of the Google Compute Engine [network](https://cloud.google.com//compute/docs/networks-and-firewalls#networks) to which the Endpoint should be peered. Private services access must already be configured for the network. If left unspecified, the Endpoint is not peered with any network. Only one of the fields, network or enable_private_service_connect, can be set. [Format](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/reference/rest/v1/networks/insert): 'projects/{project}/global/networks/{network}'. Where '{project}' is a project number, as in '12345', and '{network}' is network name. Only one of the fields, 'network' or 'privateServiceConnectConfig', can be set.
network.rationale: Configures VPC peering for the endpoint. A generic policy can mandate that this argument is set (not null) to ensure the endpoint is deployed within a private network boundary, effectively mitigating unauthorized public internet access.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: This argument simply designates the GCP project hosting the resource. Constraining it would require hardcoding specific team project IDs, which violates the generic platform policy requirement without adding intrinsic resource-level security.

region.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

traffic_split.description:
A map from a DeployedModel's id to the percentage of this Endpoint's traffic that should be forwarded to that DeployedModel.
If a DeployedModel's id is not listed in this map, then it receives no traffic.
The traffic percentage values must add up to 100, or map must be empty if the Endpoint is to not accept any traffic at a moment. See
the 'deployModel' [example](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/deployment#deploy_a_model_to_an_endpoint) and
[documentation](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1beta1/projects.locations.endpoints/deployModel) for more information.

~> **Note:** To set the map to empty, set '"{}"', apply, and then remove the field from your config.
traffic_split.rationale: This parameter configures a map determining the percentage of traffic forwarded to each deployed model. It acts strictly as an architectural rollout control governing deployment capacity and operational traffic routing, rather than serving as a direct security boundary or security perimeter.

encryption_spec.description: Customer-managed encryption key spec for an Endpoint. If set, this Endpoint and all sub-resources of this Endpoint will be secured by this key.

encryption_spec.kms_key_name.description: Required. The Cloud KMS resource identifier of the customer managed encryption key used to protect a resource. Has the form: 'projects/my-project/locations/my-region/keyRings/my-kr/cryptoKeys/my-key'. The key needs to be in the same region as where the compute resource is created.
encryption_spec.kms_key_name.rationale: This parameter directly maps to the require-encryption/CMEK archetype. A platform security policy must enforce that kms_key_name is set to a valid, non-empty value to guarantee that Vertex AI endpoints are protected using Customer-Managed Encryption Keys rather than default Google-managed keys. The policy enforces the presence of a key reference without hardcoding any specific key identifier.

predict_request_response_logging_config.description: Configures the request-response logging for online prediction.

predict_request_response_logging_config..description: If logging is enabled or not.
predict_request_response_logging_config..rationale: Controls whether online prediction requests and responses are logged. A generic policy can enforce this to be set to true across all deployments, ensuring a baseline audit trail is generated for model invocations, which is critical for incident response and security monitoring.

predict_request_response_logging_config..description: Percentage of requests to be logged, expressed as a fraction in range(0,1]
predict_request_response_logging_config..rationale: This parameter strictly defines the percentage of prediction requests to be logged. Quantitative sampling rate tuning is an operational cost-management lever and an observability trade-off, which falls entirely out of scope for core platform security policies or security enforcement boundaries.

predict_request_response_logging_config..description: BigQuery table for logging. If only given a project, a new dataset will be created with name 'logging_<endpoint-display-name>_<endpoint-id>' where will be made BigQuery-dataset-name compatible (e.g. most special characters will become underscores). If no table name is given, a new table will be created with name 'request_response_logging'

BigQuery URI to a project or table, up to 2000 characters long. When only the project is specified, the Dataset and Table is created. When the full table reference is specified, the Dataset must exist and table must not exist. Accepted forms: - BigQuery path. For example: 'bq://projectId' or 'bq://projectId.bqDatasetId' or 'bq://projectId.bqDatasetId.bqTableId'.
predict_request_response_logging_config..rationale: This field specifies the BigQuery URI used as the destination for request-response logging. It is explicitly classified as an external resource reference that requires team-specific, operational URIs to be configured, rather than acting as a platform-level security toggle or access-control mechanism.

private_service_connect_config.enable_pr.description: Required. If true, expose the IndexEndpoint via private service connect.
private_service_connect_config.enable_pr.rationale: Enabling Private Service Connect ensures the endpoint is exposed via Google's internal network rather than the public internet. A generic platform policy can mandate this boolean to enforce baseline network isolation for all deployments.

private_service_connect_config.project_a.description: A list of Projects from which the forwarding rule will target the service attachment.
private_service_connect_config.project_a.rationale: This parameter acts as a critical network-exposure control that gates which tenants can reach the private resource. A platform policy must enforce that this allowlist exists and is appropriately bounded (non-empty and not overly broad) to prevent open-to-all misconfigurations, effectively restricting unauthorized network exposure without hardcoding specific immutable project IDs.

private_service_connect_config.psc_autom.description: List of projects and networks where the PSC endpoints will be created. This field is used by Online Inference(Prediction) only.

The full name of the Google Compute Engine [network](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/networks-and-firewalls#networks). [Format](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/reference/rest/v1/networks/get): projects/{project}/global/networks/{network}.
private_service_connect_config.psc_autom.rationale: This argument requires the full name of a specific VPC network. A generic platform policy cannot enforce a hardcoded network identifier across all multi-tenant workloads, as this inherently requires team-specific context.

private_service_connect_config.psc_autom.description: Project id used to create forwarding rule.
private_service_connect_config.psc_autom.rationale: Designating the project ID for the forwarding rulerequires hardcoded, team-specific values. This falls outside the scope of generic platform policies, which must remain agnostic to individual project identities.
